stories.title: How 'Housing First' Is Helping People Leave Rough Sleeping Behind
stories.label: people
stories.summary: There's a program that flips the usual approach to homelessness on its head: instead of asking people to solve their problems before getting housing, it gives them a stable home first. It turns out that once someone has a safe place to live, everything else — health, addiction recovery, finding work — gets a lot easier to tackle. The results have been striking, with far more people staying housed long-term compared to older approaches. It's a simple idea that's proving itself in real communities right now.
stories.why_good: It's a real, already-running program with measured results helping people escape homelessness for good, not a proposal or study.

stories.title: Following Timor-Leste's Triumph, All of Southeast Asia Has Eliminated Trachoma
stories.label: health
stories.summary: The World Health Organization just certified Timor-Leste as having eliminated trachoma, the leading infectious cause of blindness worldwide. With this milestone, every single country in the WHO's Southeast Asia region has now wiped out the disease as a public health threat. That means millions fewer people will go blind from something entirely preventable. It's the result of years of quiet, steady public health work finally paying off across an entire region.
stories.why_good: A real, certified regional public health achievement that permanently protects people's eyesight.
